description:
One gate is evaluated across several issues in one invocation, so gating a wave does not require one command per issue.

## Background

`jit gate evaluate` takes one issue and one gate. Gating a set of issues that share a gate therefore means one invocation per issue, each paying whatever the checker costs even when the declared inputs have not changed between them.

Verdict reuse already exists: a gate whose declared inputs digest to a value a prior run recorded carries that run's verdict instead of executing the checker. The gap is at the command surface, not in the evaluation model.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One invocation evaluates a named gate for several named issues.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each issue receives its own recorded run and its own verdict; a failure for one issue does not suppress evaluation for the rest.
- [hard] REQ-03: The invocation reports per-issue results, and its exit status reflects whether any issue failed.
- [hard] REQ-04: Evaluation remains serialised per issue, so concurrent evaluation cannot lose a result to a per-issue lock.
title: Evaluate one gate across several issues in one invocation
